I have resolved the issue where `Model.objects.all().delete()` was generating a subquery (`DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM table)`).

### Cause
In `SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`, the compiler evaluated whether the delete query affected a single table by checking `sum(self.query.alias_refcount[t] > 0 for t in self.query.alias_map) == 1`. When `self.query.alias_map` was uninitialized (empty `{}`), this count evaluated to `0`, making `single_alias` return `False`. As a result, single-table deletions incorrectly fell back to constructing a subquery deletion.

### Solution
In [`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1412), `self.query.get_initial_alias()` is now called inside `single_alias` to ensure the base table alias is registered in `self.query.alias_map` prior to checking active table refcounts.
